title: PhonePe Becomes First Indian App to Offer Visa's Full Tokenisation Suite
excerpt: Tap to Pay, Cross Border Scan to Pay and Smart Accept debut at the Global Fintech Fest, extending the card network's tokenisation push on India's largest payments app.
body:
• PhonePe and Visa have launched three payment products at the Global Fintech Fest 2026: Tap to Pay, Cross Border Scan to Pay and Smart Accept.
  • PhonePe is the first Indian app to offer Visa's Cross Border Scan to Pay, and the first to bundle all three of the network's core consumer capabilities.
  • Tap to Pay begins rolling out September 9, 2026; cross-border QR payments will cover 14 international markets including Singapore, Japan and South Korea.
  • Smart Accept turns merchants' smartphones into card-accepting terminals, removing the cost of POS hardware for small businesses.

PhonePe and Visa have jointly unveiled three new payment products at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, in a partnership that makes PhonePe the first Indian app to offer Visa's full trio of consumer payment capabilities: online device tokenisation, tap to pay and cross-border scan to pay.

The launches — Tap to Pay, Cross Border Scan to Pay and Smart Accept — were announced on stage by leadership from both companies at the Mumbai fintech gathering, marking one of the most significant product collaborations in India's digital payments market this year.

What was launched

Tap to Pay lets Android users tokenise their Visa cards and make contactless payments at point-of-sale machines, even in low-connectivity environments. It begins rolling out in phases starting September 9, 2026.

https://x.com/YourStoryCo/status/2097973021516399019

Cross Border Scan to Pay allows users to scan Visa-supported QR codes across 14 international markets — including Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Japan, China and South Korea — removing currency-exchange friction for Indian travellers abroad. The feature rolls out to users soon.

Smart Accept is aimed at merchants rather than consumers: small businesses can accept card payments directly on their smartphones, with customers tapping physical cards or tokenised wallets against the merchant's device. It brings the cost of card-present device ownership to zero and folds card payments into PhonePe's existing QR dashboard for unified reconciliation.

Building on tokenisation

The partnership extends work the two companies began in February 2025, when Visa's device tokenisation went live on the PhonePe platform. Once a user saves a Visa card on the app, they can tap a phone to pay in stores, check out online or scan QR codes abroad without carrying a physical card.

"We are not just digitizing cards, we are establishing a new standard for borderless and cardless commerce for Indian consumers and micro-merchants alike."

— Rahul Chari, Founder and CPTO, PhonePe

"At PhonePe, our vision has always been to build technology that makes payments universally accessible, intuitive, and secure," Chari said. "Partnering with Visa is a pivotal milestone in scaling that vision globally."

Why it matters

For Visa, the deal deepens its reach into India's vast small-merchant economy through PhonePe's distribution — over 71.5 crore registered users and more than 5 crore merchants as of July 2026. For PhonePe, it adds card-network muscle to a platform built on UPI rails, and burnishes its credentials with global investors ahead of its planned public listing.

"India is at the forefront of the global digital payments revolution, and Visa is proud to be a catalyst in this transformation."

— Suresh Sethi, Group Country Manager for India and South Asia, Visa

What to watch

Execution will decide how much of this lands. Tap to Pay's phased rollout and the cross-border feature's market-by-market activation both depend on bank and merchant readiness. But the direction is clear: India's payments giants are racing to own the traveller's wallet and the neighbourhood kirana's counter in a single app — and this partnership puts PhonePe at the front of that race.
